card.title: Those Exact Words
card.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note says I'm 'welcome for now.' Should I unpack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I meant until your flat's repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'for now' instead of 'until the repairs'? Is your welcome wearing out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross it out. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But 'for now' was there before I complained. What happens when I stop asking?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 isolates for-now wording, A3 contrasts it with a repair deadline, and A5 treats removal of that same phrase as evidence its original meaning persists.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's repair explanation gives A3 the alternative wording; B4's deletion makes A5 focus on what was written before complaint.

relationship.evidence: B2 clearly grants temporary accommodation and B4 corrects the note to reassure A.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's correction as evidence about the original wording rather than accepting the corrected welcome.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes unpacking after a welcome note, and B2 supplies the flat-repair context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's before-I-complained distinction follows B4's visible correction and sustains the exact phrase fixation.
